geometry_edits.rationale: Align the notch to the verified frontage/access side to strengthen entry legibility.
Increase the breadth of the frontage carve so the ground response reads as a true public void.
Deepen the notch to improve access-side openness while keeping the hall continuous.

graph_edits.rationale: Keep the public threshold aligned to the verified access edge and reinforce the entry seam on the frontage side.
Widen the notch slightly to make the access-facing void more legible without breaking the dominant bar.
Deepen the public carve just enough to create a clearer ground response while preserving the main mass.

rationale: The candidate reads coherently in all four views as one dominant long bar with a stepped roof/profile rather than a collection of colliding parts. The primary mass is legible, the hierarchy is clear, and the silhouette is sufficiently resolved for an early gymnasium massing. The main weakness is that the access-edge response is only modest: the mass sits on the parcel but does not carve a strong public void or court toward the verified frontage, so the ground condition feels more sealed than inviting. Still, the section logic is compatible with a compact hall and subordinate threshold rather than an unrelated sculptural object, so the program passes.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise sports massing with a clear horizontal datum and a controlled public edge can support gymnasium-like program.
Dispersed low pavilions and bridging/canopy logic suggest a way to keep the hall readable while adding support pieces.
Faceted low-rise volume with a distinct opening demonstrates a viable public cut in an otherwise compact mass.
A broad pavilion and foreground court show how a sports building can address access with a legible open ground figure.
A singular roof profile over a subordinate base supports the idea of one dominant hall with a lighter ancillary threshold.

warnings: Open-space figure is underdeveloped relative to the access edge; consider a clearer notch/court/undercut toward frontage.
The stepped roof is coherent, but it is close to a generic terraced datum; stronger daylight/span expression would improve program legibility.
